en.title: Northeast snow this weekend: 16 resorts have cover, but it is thin
en.description: Only 16 Northeast resorts hold snow on 18 November, with Tuckerman Ravine leading at 38 cm. No new snow forecast through Saturday.
en.lede: This weekend in the Northeast, your ski choice is narrow: go to the highest slopes at Tuckerman Ravine or Stratton if you want to ski on snow, or stay home. Thin early-season cover and no new snow in the forecast mean conditions are fragile and shrinking.

p: Tuckerman Ravine leads the Northeast with 38 cm (15 in) on upper slopes. Stratton ranks second with 20 cm (8 in) at the summit. These two stand alone; the remaining 14 resorts with measurable cover hold very little, and most of the region is bare ground.

Snow cover across the Northeast today blankets only 670 square kilometres. Two days ago it covered 6410 square kilometres. That collapse shows how fast early-season snow melts when air warms and no fresh powder arrives. By Saturday, only around 90 square kilometres will hold snow, spread across just four resorts.

sections.h: Height decides who skis this weekend
p: At Stratton, the base sits at 607 m (1,991 ft) where the air is too warm for snow to survive. Mid-mountain (895 m / 2,936 ft) has zero depth. Only the summit at 1183 m (3,881 ft) keeps any snow at all—a thin 2 cm (1 in). The freezing level tonight rises to 3290–3610 m (10,800–11,850 ft), so cold air is well above the ski terrain.

Tuckerman Ravine's upper slopes fare better at 38 cm, but snow map see snow presence, not safe skiing depth. Rocks, stumps and rough ground still poke through. South-facing slopes are thinnest; north-facing slopes hold more. Any afternoon sun will soften what little cover exists.

sections.h: What the forecast means for your trip
p: Zero new snow is predicted for Thursday, Friday or Saturday. The region will see no precipitation, so the 38 cm at Tuckerman Ravine and 20 cm at Stratton will only shrink or harden as night temperatures drop and day temperatures rise. By Sunday, cover will be even thinner than today.
This is typical for mid-November in the Northeast. The season is so young that snow survives only on the highest, shadiest terrain. Patience pays off: snow will come, but this is not the week.

sections.h: How to stay safe on thin snow
p: If you drive to the mountains this weekend, stay on groomed, patrolled runs at the highest elevations. Rocks hide under thin cover. South-facing slopes are especially risky—the snow there is weakest and shortest. Off-piste terrain is off-limits until depth and stability improve.

Before you go off-piste anywhere, read the official avalanche bulletin for your area. Early-season snow may slide or collapse without warning. Many Northeast resorts may not open lifts at all if snow is too sparse; check the resort website for lift status and opening hours before you leave home.

sections.h: Make a smart choice for the weekend
p: If skiing is your goal, drive to Tuckerman Ravine or Stratton. Both have more snow than anywhere else in the region. Arrive early to ski north-facing terrain while it is firm; afternoon warmth softens what little exists. Bring layers so you can adjust as the day warms and your activity heats up.

If depth matters to you, Tuckerman Ravine's 38 cm upper slopes give you the best odds. If you value high elevation and cooler conditions that hold snow longer, Stratton's 1183 m summit is your play. Either way, confirm before you go. Sparse snow may limit or close operations.

advice: Drive to Tuckerman Ravine (38 cm on upper slopes) or Stratton (20 cm at the summit) if you want to ski; all other Northeast resorts are thin or bare.
Hunt north-facing slopes and summit terrain where snow lasts longest as day–night temperature swings melt and refreeze the surface.
Avoid off-piste runs entirely until snow depth rises; thin cover hides rocks and rough ground. Check the official avalanche bulletin before you enter the backcountry.
Confirm lift openings on the resort website before you travel; with only four resorts forecast to hold snow by Saturday, many may not operate.
Ski groomed, patrolled runs only. Arrive early to ski firm snow on cool north-facing slopes; afternoon sun softens and thins what little cover exists.
